key_insight: A DSL-guided multi-agent LLM workflow can improve inverse materials design by grounding natural-language rules in symbolic predicates and statistical evidence.
engineering_relevance: This approach offers a scalable way to search for high-performance perovskite oxides without task-specific training data, while keeping the design logic interpretable.
method: Translate design rules from natural language into chemistry DSL predicates.
Use accumulated materials data to test, validate, and refine rules during iterative design.
Deploy the ORCHESTRA multi-agent framework for inverse design of double perovskite oxides under multiple property targets.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that symbolic predicates helped identify unsupported rules, validate new rules, and improve the rule store over iterative design cycles, with better performance than natural-language-only rules for harder targets.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of the DSL predicates and underlying materials data, so weak or biased rule encoding could limit design reliability.
paper_title: Symbolic Predicate-Guided Language Agents for Inverse Design of Perovskite Oxides
